chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"Any food that you have specified with a measure (kayl) is not suitable for sale by estimation (mujazafah), and this is among what is disliked in the sale of food."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling food by estimation if it is defined by a specific measure?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that 'mujazafah' (sale by estimation) is prohibited for food items previously defined by a specific measure (*kayl*), distinguishing this from general uncertainty. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on eliminating *gharar* (uncertainty) in commercial transactions to ensure fairness and prevent dispute among buyers and sellers. It reflects the broader principle that precise measurement is required when the commodity's quantity is already established, thereby safeguarding economic justice.
